sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS utility_patent_count
FROM (
    SELECT p.patent_id
    FROM PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS p
    JOIN PATENTS.PATENTS.CITATIONS c
        ON p.patent_id = c.cited_patent_id
    JOIN PATENTS.PATENTS.PUBLICATIONS cp
        ON c.citing_patent_id = cp.patent_id
    WHERE p.patent_type = 'Utility'
      AND YEAR(p.grant_date) = 2010
      -- forward citation must occur within 10 years of the original patent's filing/application date
      AND DATEDIFF('day', p.filing_date, cp.grant_date) <= 3650
    GROUP BY p.patent_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) = 1
) AS filtered_patents;
reasoning: The query first isolates utility patents granted in 2010 from the PUBLICATIONS table. It then joins to a citations table to find forward citations and joins again to the PUBLICATIONS table to obtain the grant date of each citing patent. The DATEDIFF filter keeps only citations that occur within a 10‑year (≈3650 days) window after the original patent's filing date. Grouping by the original patent ID and applying HAVING COUNT(*) = 1 ensures exactly one qualifying forward citation. Finally, the outer SELECT counts the distinct patents that satisfy all conditions.
